latest.title: AGM Statement
latest.content:
22 Sep 2026 07:00

Crimson Tide PLC
22 September 2026
22 September 2026
Crimson Tide plc
(“Crimson Tide”, the “Company” or the “Group”)
AGM statement
At the Annual General Meeting of Crimson Tide today at 1.00 pm, Chris Fielding, Chair of the Company, will make the following statement:
“I am pleased to report that the Group has made a good start to the financial year ending 30 April 2027 and trading is in line with market expectations for FY27.
Five new customers have been contracted since the start of the year, each of which is now live on the mpro5 platform. In addition, three existing customers have agreed 12-month contract extensions, demonstrating continued confidence in the platform and our customer success model. These wins reflect the evolution of our go-to-market strategy. We are increasingly targeting smaller, faster-to-deploy opportunities alongside larger enterprise contracts. A standardised product, lower entry price and shorter sales cycle allow us to win more customers, deploy them more quickly and grow them from within.
Contracted monthly recurring revenue stood at £0.4 million at the date of this statement. Although forecast churn has moderated the rate of growth, new customer wins and expansion within the existing customer base have returned the Group to a positive MRR trajectory.
Our repositioning of mpro5 as one connected platform for frontline compliance, supported by the new brand and website launched in May and by increased investment in marketing this year, is starting to gain traction. The pipeline continues to build and, importantly, to convert.
Cash as at 21 September 2026 amounted to £1.5 million (£1.3 million at the date of last AGM on 29
th
October 2025 and £2.1 million at 30 April 2026). This reflects the normal timing of cash receipts and expenditure across the Group together with ongoing investment in product development and growth initiatives.
We anticipate announcing our interim results for the half year to 31 October 2026 before the end of November.”

Contract Extensions with Public Sector Customers
Crimson Tide plc (AIM: TIDE), the provider of the mpro5 operational compliance platform, is pleased to announce that it has agreed 12-month extensions to two existing public sector contracts, representing combined annual recurring revenue ("ARR") of £211k.
Both customers use mpro5 to digitalise routine inspection, servicing and compliance activity across large, geographically dispersed estates, replacing paper-based records with real-time data capture and giving central teams consistent visibility of standards across all locations.
Commenting on the extensions, Jon Clarke, CEO of Crimson Tide plc, said:
"We are pleased that both of these customers have chosen to extend their contracts. Public sector organisations face the same operational challenge as our largest commercial customers - maintaining consistent standards across a large and varied estate - and

company_30s.what_they_do: Crimson Tide delivers outsourced support services to the public sector – from cleaning and maintenance to facility management and basic IT support.  The focus is on long‑term contracts with NHS trusts, local councils and educational institutions.
company_30s.why_they_matter: Public‑sector service contracts are usually multi‑year, low‑competition, and cash‑flow stable.  As the UK government pushes for efficiency, providers that can deliver reliable, low‑cost support are in demand.  Crimson Tide sits in that niche, offering a repeatable revenue stream that can scale as it wins more contracts.
company_30s.current_state: The firm has just broken into profitability for FY26 after a loss the year before.  It is still a small player, but its recent contract extensions and new wins suggest a pivot toward growth.  The share price is trading very low, indicating the market has not yet priced in this turnaround.

rns_narrative: The company’s latest filings show a series of contract extensions with public‑sector customers – including a multi‑year deal with Cadent and a new win with APCOA Parking – that should lock in revenue for the next 12–18 months.
FY26 results reveal a modest profit before tax, a clear turnaround from the previous year’s loss, signalling that cost controls are working and cash flow is improving.
The director disclosures and shareholding updates suggest that key executives remain invested, which is a good sign of confidence in the business model.

crowd_tape.dominant_theme: Quiet optimism – investors are still silent, but the few bullish posts focus on the new contracts and profit turnaround.
crowd_tape.bull_narrative: Bulls point to the firm’s ability to win and extend public‑sector contracts, arguing that the business model is resilient and that the recent profit shows it can become a stable cash‑generating entity.
crowd_tape.bear_narrative: Bears worry that the company’s scale is still tiny, that it may struggle to deliver on new contracts, and that a single contract loss could wipe out the gains made in FY26.
crowd_tape.sentiment_shift: Sentiment has barely moved – the chatter is mostly bullish but very limited.  The silence gives a contrarian edge because the market hasn’t yet reacted.

whats_happening_now.attention_check: Google Trends for the ticker is flat, meaning there is no pre‑existing hype.  A news hit could produce a surprise bounce.

near_term_catalysts: Quarterly earnings release – a clear profit or revenue beat would confirm the turnaround.
Public‑sector contract renewal announcements – each extension should add a predictable cash‑flow block.
Volume spikes on announcement days – a sudden lift in trading volume can signal a breakout.
Any regulatory approval or audit clearance – would remove a potential hurdle to scaling.
expect_next.watch_for: Look for a 20–30% rise in volume on the day of a contract announcement, and a price break above the recent high of the 20‑day moving average.  A sustained move 5% higher than the current low would confirm mean‑reversion.
expect_next.timing_regime: The share appears to be in the early stage of a crash‑recovery cycle.  The APEX score suggests a tight compression that could snap once a catalyst arrives.  Patience is required – a single announcement is unlikely to produce a full bounce; a series of positive signals will.

buy_vs_sell.bull_case: The stock is likely down 70‑90% from its peak, giving a huge upside if it rebounds to even half of the pre‑crash level – a 200% gain is realistic.  The recent profit and contract wins are the key catalysts that should drive a mean‑reversion.  The asymmetry is clear: a small loss if the contracts fail, but a large win if the turnaround sticks.
buy_vs_sell.bear_case: If the firm fails to deliver on new contracts, or if a key public‑sector customer pulls out, the share could fall further, wiping out the recovery.  The company’s small scale and thin margins mean it could struggle if costs rise or if it needs additional capital.
buy_vs_sell.risk_reward: Potential loss: 80% of the current price (if the company collapses).  Potential gain: 200% (if it recovers to half its pre‑crash level).  The reward is more than twice the risk, making the trade attractive for a contrarian.

playbook.if_bullish: Enter on a volume spike that confirms a breakout above the recent high.  Size the position to 5–10% of your portfolio, set a stop 10% below the breakout point, and trail the stop as the price moves higher.
playbook.if_watching: Wait for a contract renewal announcement or a profit beat.  A clear 20% volume jump on that day, combined with a 5% price move above the 20‑day MA, is a strong entry signal.
playbook.if_passing: If the company is delisted or files for bankruptcy, exit immediately.  Otherwise, maintain a bullish stance.

ai_insights.bottom_line: Crimson Tide sits at the bottom of a deep crash, but new public‑sector contracts and a first‑year profit signal a possible explosive mean‑reversion – a high‑reward, low‑risk play for contrarian traders.
